# Simple CLI

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

This PR extends the functionality of the CLI to not only support disassembly (of either spi/generic programs) but also to execute them until halt or the first host call.

Follow up:
- [ ] Supply ecalli execution trace to perform full execution (details: https://github.com/tomusdrw/JIPs/blob/td-jip6-ecalliloggin/JIP-6.md)

## Walkthrough

This PR moves build outputs from build/ to dist/, updates package.json, tsconfig.json, asconfig.json, and build scripts to the new dist layout, and adds a compiler build target. It introduces assembly/api-types.ts with VM I/O data types and relocates InitialChunk/InitialPage/VmInput/VmOutput imports to that module. It adds runJAM in assembly/api-utils.ts and a pvmMain SPI entrypoint (exporting result_ptr/result_len) in assembly/index-compiler.ts. Several AssemblyScript signatures/types were tightened (pc → u32, u8[] usage), assembly/index.ts now re-exports api-internal broadly, and the CLI (bin/index.ts) was replaced with disassemble/run subcommands.

## Possibly related PRs

- tomusdrw/anan-as PR 85: Alters the same assembly modules (api-utils.ts and related) by adding/adjusting public VM utility functions and exported types.  
- tomusdrw/anan-as PR 78: Refactors VM execution flow and VM I/O handling, overlapping changes to executeProgram/runVm and the movement/renaming of VM I/O types.  
- tomusdrw/anan-as PR 93: Updates CLI and utility scripts (bin/index.ts and related), aligning with the new disassemble/run subcommand structure and flag handling.

**`runJAM` silently loses output results containing zero bytes or spanning chunks due to `getOutputChunks` zero-stripping.**

`getOutputChunks` terminates chunks at any zero byte (api-internal.ts:78), splitting contiguous output. When a JAM program returns output containing zeros or split across chunks, `runJAM` cannot find it because the extraction logic (line 133) requires the entire pointer range `[ptr_start, ptr_end)` to fit within a single chunk. Results fail silently with an empty result. Additionally, casting pointer offsets to `i32` (line 136) risks truncation if `ptr_start` or `ptr_end` exceed `INT32_MAX`.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@assembly/api-utils.ts` around lines 117 - 139, runJAM currently assumes the
full JAM output range [ptr_start, ptr_end) sits inside a single chunk and casts
offsets to i32, so outputs containing zero bytes or spanning multiple chunks
from getOutputChunks are lost or risk truncation; fix runJAM by reconstructing
the result across all output.memory chunks that intersect the pointer range
instead of requiring a single chunk: iterate output.memory, for each chunk
compute the overlapping slice using safe Number (or i64-aware) arithmetic for s
= max(ptr_start, start) - start and e = min(ptr_end, end) - start,
copy/concatenate chunk.data.slice(s,e) into a growing Uint8Array (or push into
an array then concat), stop once accumulated length equals ptr_end - ptr_start,
and remove the <i32> casts so you don’t truncate large pointers; ensure bounds
checks for negative or out-of-range pointers (ptr_start >= ptr_end still returns
empty).
```

🌐 Web query:

`Biome files.includes glob pattern negation "!" semantics documentation`

💡 Result:

In Biome config, `files.includes` is an **ordered list of glob patterns**; entries that start with `!` are **negated patterns (exceptions)** that *exclude* matches. Negations are applied **in order**, so you can create “exceptions to exceptions” by re-including later patterns. [1][2]

Key semantics for `!` patterns:

- **Negated patterns can’t be used alone**; they must act as exceptions to a prior positive match (typically `**`). [2]
- If you use a negated pattern, you should **include `**` first**, otherwise the negation may match nothing (because nothing was included in the first place). [1][2]
- **Order matters**: later patterns can override earlier ones (include → exclude → re-include → exclude, etc.). [2]
- Folder handling: to include all files under a folder, use `folder/**`; to ignore a folder (and all contents), `!folder` is enough (and recommended). [2]

Example from the docs:

```json
{
  "files": {
    "includes": ["**", "!**/*.test.js", "**/special.test.js", "!test"]
  }
}
```

This means: include everything → exclude `*.test.js` → re-include `special.test.js` → exclude anything under `test/`. [2]

Sources: Biome “Configure Biome” guide (files/includes + negation) [1], Biome configuration reference (detailed order/exception semantics + glob syntax notes) [2].

---

🌐 Web query:

`Biome configuration "!dist" exclude pattern subtree files`

💡 Result:

To exclude a whole `dist` folder subtree in **Biome**, use a **negated glob** in `files.includes` (and make sure `**` comes first):

### Ignore `dist/` at the project root
```json
{
  "files": {
    "includes": ["**", "!dist"]
  }
}
```
`!dist` ignores the `dist` folder **and all files under it** (without needing `/**`). [1][2]

### Ignore any `dist/` folder anywhere (e.g., in monorepos)
```json
{
  "files": {
    "includes": ["**", "!**/dist"]
  }
}
```
This excludes every `dist` directory regardless of location. [3][2]

Notes:
- Negated patterns (`!…`) only work as “exceptions” if you include `**` first; otherwise they may not match anything. [1][3]
- Prefer `!dist` over `!dist/**` to avoid traversing the folder (better performance). [2]
